question: Forest fires are on the increase in Europe as a result of climate change. The fires are becoming more intense, more frequent and more widespread. In 2022, 837 212 hectares were burnt in the EU, including almost 72 000 hectares in France.

Although the EU has stepped up its response capacity through the rescEU civil protection mechanism, including Canadair-type water-bomber planes, it is still dependent on a limited number of manufacturers and does not have enough industrial capacity to quickly renew and strengthen its fleet.
This dependence is posing major challenges for civil security and the strategic autonomy of the EU in the face of heightened climate risks. With the above in mind: 1.
What action is the Commission intending to take to develop EU manufacturing capacity for Canadair-type water-bomber planes or equivalent aircraft?
What EU funding is the Commission planning to deploy to support research and development in this area, as well as the manufacturing of these strategic aircraft?
What measures is it planning to propose with a view to stepping up cooperation, pooling of resources and solidarity among Member States in the face of natural disasters?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (28.8.2026) The Commission shares the concerns about the increasing frequency and intensity of wildfires linked to climate change and is preparing a new EU Integrated Framework on Climate Resilience. It will aim to establish a more anticipatory, comprehensive and coherent approach to climate preparedness and resilience at EU and Member State level, including for EU economy.

Since 2019, the EU has started developing the future permanent rescEU1 fleet, financing the acquisition of 12 new firefighting airplanes and five helicopters. While the technical specifications of assets remain under the responsibility of Member States, the Commission is working with them and with the industry to identify and closely monitor the development of potential new suitable European projects.

The Commission will continue to mobilise relevant EU programmes, including Horizon Europe, InvestEU and the Cohesion Policy funds, to support research, innovation and, where eligible, industrial investments contributing to develop an EU manufacturing of water-bomber aircraft.

The Commission will also continue to strengthen cooperation among Member States through the Union Civil Protection Mechanism2 by expanding rescEU capacities, improving interoperability, promoting joint training and exercises, and reinforcing prevention, preparedness and solidarity.

In the context of the negotiations on the next Multiannual Financial Framework (2028–2034) and on the Commission proposal for a Regulation on the Union Civil Protection3, the support of the European Parliament will be essential to ensure the effective implementation of activities aiming at building a more resilient and better-prepared Europe.
